subject: Follow-up: Availability exceptions + cutover plan for Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira.patel@kestrelhealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: tom.wu@kestrelhealth.com, contracts@kestrelhealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Order form redlines — availability exceptions and cutover window

Hi Olga,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. Attached is a marked-up version (Kestrel_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) with three items we need clearer language on before we can sign: uptime measurement and credits, permitted maintenance windows during our quarterly clinical cutover, and the cutover/upgrade blackout period for model migrations.

High-level asks:
- Uptime target: we need 99.95% per month (not 99.9%) for the hosted endpoints supporting our production workflows.
- Credits: please add a defined credit table (hours of downtime -> % credit) rather than only referencing "service credits" in Schedule A.
- Maintenance: we need a guaranteed advance notice of 14 days for planned maintenance that might affect live inference, and a maximum of one maintenance event >2 hours per quarter during our clinical cutover months (May/Nov).
- Cutover blackout: during our migration windows (typically first two Mondays of May and Nov), we ask that you not perform model weight upgrades or instance rebalancing during 00:00-12:00 PT.

We appreciate that some of these are negotiable — Samira and I are open to a pragmatic middle ground, but we need precise contract language for our internal risk and regulatory reviewers. Please route to ops and legal and let us know a proposed countertext.

Best,
Samira Patel
Head of IT & Clinical Ops
Kestrel Health

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@kestrelhealth.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form redlines — availability exceptions and cutover window

Samira — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Jonas (legal) and Marcus (ops). High level response before formal redline:

- Uptime: our standard hosted SLA in the Order Form is 99.9% monthly. Moving to 99.95% materially changes capacity and cost assumptions. We can offer 99.95% for a dedicated reservation or with a small "premium" on the committed monthly fee.
- Credits: we can provide a clear credit table tied to monthly uptime percentage bands; will propose language.
- Maintenance notice: 14 days notice is reasonable for non-emergency planned maintenance; we typically commit to 7 days.
- Cutover blackout: we can accept a customer-specified blackout if scheduled in advance, but need to define permitted emergency maintenance and a process for mutually agreed exceptions.

Next steps: Jonas, can you draft countertext for the Order Form (Schedule A) that: (1) proposes a credit table, (2) allows for a 99.95% path tied to reserved capacity or fee, and (3) defines a 14-day notice for planned maintenance with a carve-out for emergency security patches. Marcus, can you confirm operational constraints for honoring a hard blackout during model weight swaps.

Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, samira.patel@kestrelhealth.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form redlines — availability exceptions and cutover window

Samira / Olga / team — attaching draft counter language in the order form (see link: https://redwood.app/drive/KD-2026-039/orderform-v3) and inline highlights below. Key legal points: 

1) Availability measurement and credit table (Schedule A) — proposed monthly uptime bands: >=99.95%: no credit; 99.5%-99.95%: 5% monthly fee credit; 99.0%-99.499%: 15% monthly fee credit; <99.0%: 30% monthly fee credit. For customers that require guaranteed 99.95% we have a ConversionAddendum that requires dedicated capacity and a 10% fee uplift.

2) Maintenance windows — proposed change: Planned Maintenance: Redwood will provide at least fourteen (14) calendar days' advance notice for any Planned Maintenance reasonably expected to affect availability. Planned Maintenance that affects availability will be scheduled in a continuous window not to exceed four (4) hours per maintenance event, and not more than two (2) such events in any calendar quarter (exceptions allowed by mutual written agreement).

3) Cutover blackout — proposed clause: Customer may designate up to two (2) blackout windows per calendar year (each a continuous twelve (12) hour window) during which Redwood shall not perform model upgrades or instance rebalancing that would affect availability, provided Customer gives at least sixty (60) days' notice for each such designation. Emergency maintenance and security patches are excluded but Redwood will make reasonable efforts to avoid performing such actions during the blackout and will notify Customer as soon as practicable.

Jonas — notes on risks: the 60-day notice is to allow capacity planning; we cannot accept a recurring ad-hoc blackout with short notice without dedicated reservations.

Marcus — pls confirm if 4-hour per event limit is operationally feasible for larger model rollouts.

— Jonas
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com, samira.patel@kestrelhealth.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form redlines — availability exceptions and cutover window

Samira / team — operational confirmation and suggested pragmatic tweaks: 

- 4-hour window per maintenance event: feasible for routine infra patches and smaller model swaps. For large model weight migrations that require rolling restarts across multiple AZs, an event may take longer; propose language to allow a single extended maintenance event (up to 8 hours) per calendar year for major upgrades, with the two-event / quarter limit still applying to routine maintenance.

- Cutover blackout: 12-hour blackout windows are OK if we get 60 days' advance notice and a little flexibility for emergency security fixes. For guaranteed 99.95% the customer should be on Dedicated (or pay the uplift).

- Credits table: ops prefers credits be capped at 30% of monthly service fees and that credits be the sole remedy for availability. Also recommend adding a paragraph that scheduled maintenance notified within >14 days does not count toward downtime for credit calculations.

Action: I will prepare an operational appendix (Availability_Schedule_Proposed.xlsx) showing how maintenance events are scheduled and how credits would apply across a sample month. Please confirm by EOD if this aligns and I will finalize timings for the cutover model migration runbook.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: Samira Patel <samira.patel@kestrelhealth.com>, contracts@kestrelhealth.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form redlines — availability exceptions and cutover window

Samira — thanks for the patience while we pulled ops/legal together. Summary of proposed compromise for Kestrel to review: 

1) Availability: keep base hosted SLA at 99.9% (included in Order Form). Offer an Optional "99.95% Commitment" via ConversionAddendum that requires either Dedicated capacity or a 10% monthly fee uplift.

2) Credits: include the credit bands as proposed by Jonas, capped at 30% of monthly fees; credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability failures.

3) Planned maintenance: commit to 14 calendar days' notice for planned maintenance that may affect availability; standard event cap of 4 hours per event and no more than two such events per calendar quarter.

4) Major upgrades carve-out: allow one (1) extended maintenance event per calendar year up to 8 hours for model migrations/major upgrades; this event will be notified at least 30 days in advance. Events notified with >=14 days' notice will not be counted toward downtime for credits.

5) Cutover blackout: allow Customer to designate up to two (2) twelve (12) hour blackout windows per year with 60 days' notice; Redwood will avoid upgrades during those windows except for emergency security patches (Redwood will notify and coordinate).

Next steps: If Kestrel can accept the above, Jonas will incorporate the language into the attached Order Form PDF and Marcus will share the operational runbook for the migration. If Kestrel wants 99.95% without Dedicated, we need to discuss the uplift and capacity commitment.

Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments referenced: Kestrel_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf, Availability_Schedule_Proposed.xlsx
